newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS REGAIN EIGHT POINT LEAD IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS REGAIN EIGHT POINT LEAD IN ITALY.

text.p: Striker Christian Vieri scored twice on Saturday as European Cup holders Juventus beat Roma 3-0 and restored their eight point league lead in Italy.

Vieri, thrust into the front line of a below-strength Juventus, scored in the 28th and 44th minutes to dismiss any notion that the absence of injured striker Alessandro del Piero and suspended Croat Alen Boksic had weakened the team.
Nicola Amoruso scored the third in the 85th.

Juventus, whose match was brought forward from the usual Sunday slot to allow more time to prepare for Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final second leg against Norway's Rosenborg, have 48 points after 24 matches.
But second-placed Parma, more realistically chasing a place in the European Cup as runners-up, can cut the gap to five points if they beat third placed Inter later.
That match was brought forward due to Inter's UEFA Cup commitments against Anderlecht of Belgium.
Parma have 40 points and Inter, who drew 0-0 with Juventus at the San Siro last weekend, are on 38.
Struggling AC Milan, in 12th place before Saturday's match, overcame Cup Winners' Cup hopefuls Fiorentina 2-0 to leapfrog them, Napoli and Lazio and move up to ninth place.

French international midfielder Marcel Desailly headed in the first in the 61st minute from close range. Second half substitute Demetrio Albertini scored the second with an 89th minute penalty after George Weah was felled.
